name: Independent power-on and source readiness
prerequisites: Correctly flashed custom PCB on a protected regulated standalone supply; safe bench output fixture; all ST-LINK/Nucleo/diagnostic leads removed.
procedure: With the programming interface fully disconnected, remove and reapply the intended operating power.
After the device starts, select microphone with E11 and provide a normal room sound.
Repeat the cold start a further two times without reconnecting programming equipment.
expected: Three successive starts without a laptop, serial console, manual reset or reflash.
Microphone audio becomes audible and the local source controls respond.
gate: R24 untethered USB-C startup has been operator reported; intended battery supply requires independent qualification.

name: Ambient microphone, dynamic level and local control
prerequisites: Safe bench speaker or output fixture, measured or controlled acoustic stimulus, microphone mode selected.
procedure: Present recorded or live speech at 0.5 m; document source and listening distance.
Repeat from 2–3 m under the same environment and then add a representative traffic/pedestrian ambience recording.
Rotate encoder three detents clockwise and back; tap E10 twice to mute and restore audio.
Repeat with a quieter and louder stimulus, maintaining a safe output level.
expected: Nearby speech and background environmental audio are audible and distant pickup is recorded honestly with limitations.
Volume changes in the intended direction without repeated reverse steps; mute changes state on each intentional touch.
Output remains bounded under the deliberately changed input level; measured levels and any distortion are recorded.
gate: R26 ambient DSP has portable tests; acoustic sensitivity, noise and SPL need physical evidence.

name: Bluetooth audio and link interruption
prerequisites: Compatible Bluetooth phone and a known recording, approved safe output level.
procedure: Touch E8, pair or reconnect the phone, and play a known speech/music clip.
Pause and resume playback.
Disconnect the phone source, reconnect and play again without resetting the hearing prototype.
expected: Bluetooth programme material is audible when selected and playback follows the phone.
Connection interruption does not crash the device and playback resumes without reflashing.
gate: R24 playback was operator reported; source reconnection and latency need repeatable bench records.

name: Induction-loop telecoil reception and idle noise
prerequisites: Induction-loop test fixture, safe isolated 2 kHz stimulus and output-level instrumentation.
procedure: Touch E9 to select telecoil and enable the 2 kHz loop stimulus.
Reduce and restore the loop signal to compare wanted-signal output.
Remove the loop stimulus entirely, observe residual hiss, and restore the same signal.
expected: 2 kHz is audible from the telecoil using the PCM LOW16 path, with the filter enabled.
Wanted signal returns promptly; idle hiss and weak-signal performance are reported from observations rather than presumed solved.
gate: LOW16 and FILTER ON worked in operator R23/R24 tests; R26 adaptive TC reduction is unverified on physical hardware.

name: Unexpected control order and bounce resistance
prerequisites: Safe audio stimulus for each source and available phone and loop apparatus.
procedure: Select E11 microphone, E8 Bluetooth, E9 telecoil, and E11 again in that order.
Touch each of E8, E9, E10 and E11 intentionally five times while observing the resulting mode.
Rotate encoder five detents each way during audio and verify no spurious direction reversal.
expected: Each intentional touch causes only the intended source/mute change, with any missed/double inputs recorded.
Encoder adjustments are monotonic and the device remains responsive during source changes.
gate: Physical control hardware is operator reported working; demonstrate repeatability without a serial console.

name: Closed-loop gain adaptation and interference rejection
prerequisites: Microphone input with fixed reference distance, reproducible quiet/louder stimuli and a safe output fixture.
procedure: Play the same short speech/ambient sample at two defined levels while remaining in microphone mode.
Repeat the fixed sample to see whether the automatic gain and noise response settles without oscillation.
Describe the observable response of adaptive output without assigning semantic labels to learned clusters.
expected: A reproducible input-dependent change in listening level or noise behaviour is observable and documented.
No unsupported claim is made that the three unlabelled acoustic clusters classify cars or people.
gate: R26 implements a three-prototype unsupervised learner, but the hardware response must be independently verified.

name: Power-cycle, source-loss and continuity robustness
prerequisites: All external sources at a safe level, independent operating power, device running normally.
procedure: Select microphone and operate it continuously while changing volume and mute.
Interrupt Bluetooth programme audio, then restore it and select microphone again.
Power-cycle the custom PCB with the Nucleo and programming interface disconnected; observe return to service.
Record any glitch, spontaneous mute, dropout, lockup or unexpected startup behaviour.
expected: Normal operation continues or recovers without reset or reprogramming except for the requested power cycle.
All failures and recovery times are recorded; the audio path does not rely on debug connectivity.
gate: Recorded black-box runtime and recovery results are required; do potentially damaging tests only after routine demonstration with permission.
